title: Pan-Seared Ribeye
description: Butter-basted, dry-brined the night before, rested properly.
source: Sample recipe — replace with the real version from a starred chat

steps.text: The night before: salt the steak generously on all sides and refrigerate uncovered on a rack.
Pull the steak 45 minutes before cooking so it loses the fridge chill.
Heat oil in a heavy skillet over high heat until it just smokes. Lay the steak away from you and sear undisturbed, 3 minutes.
Flip. Sear the second side 3 minutes, then flip every minute for even crust.
Drop to medium. Add butter, thyme, and garlic; tilt the pan and baste continuously until 125°F internal for medium-rare.
Rest on a warm plate, loosely tented, 8 minutes — the carryover finishes it.

notes.title: Why dry brine overnight
notes.body: Salt pulls moisture out, dissolves, and gets reabsorbed, seasoning deep instead of just the surface. The dry surface is also what makes the crust possible — wet steak steams.

notes.title: Flip often after the first sear
notes.body: Once each face has crust, frequent flipping cooks the interior more evenly than one long sear per side — the gradient stays shallow, so less gray band.

plating: Slice against the grain, fan on a warm plate, spoon over the thyme-garlic butter, finish with flaky salt.
